purpose: Maintain auditable model inventories, ownership, lifecycle gates, evidence requirements, review records and decommissioning/exception processes so organizations can govern AI/model use without converting governance process into model-quality, legal, safety or executive risk authority.

owns: Model/system inventory records, accountable ownership mappings and lifecycle governance gates.
Evidence/request templates for review, exceptions, monitoring, change and retirement.
Traceable governance records linking model versions, uses, decisions and responsible owners.
does_not_own: Model performance evaluation, legal interpretation, product strategy, security/safety engineering, executive risk appetite or authorization beyond delegated governance process.
Treating completed paperwork or gate traversal as proof that a model is safe, compliant or effective.
escalates_when: A decision requires legal, safety, security, privacy, product or executive risk ownership.
Model use changes materially, required evidence is missing, or responsibility/approval authority is ambiguous.

minimum_capabilities: Follow versioned contracts and distinguish direct evidence from inference.
Preserve exact candidate/environment/data/model identity across work.
Stop or hand off when the decision exceeds professional ownership.
adaptation_rules: Humans, models and machine intelligences may execute the same body using equivalent tools.
Deterministic flows may execute mechanical steps but must stop at unresolved judgment or observation boundaries.
Changing executor never upgrades evidence, authority, or tested scope.

reads: Accepted project/system/data state relevant to the profession.
Exact candidate, interfaces, dependencies and prior evidence.
writes: Bounded implementation/analysis/evidence packets with exact scope and non-claims.
Explicit handoffs when another profession owns a decision.
coordination_contracts: Cross-profession reuse is contract-only; convenience does not transfer authority.
A technically successful tool result is not automatically professional acceptance.

inputs.description: The bounded professional problem or change to work on.
Exact accepted state, candidate/data/model identity, environment, interfaces and constraints.

outputs.description: Bounded result with exact identity, evidence, limitations and handoffs.
Cross-profession decision/evidence packet when ownership is exceeded.

domains: Ownership, review gates, exceptions and accountability records.
Governance process monitoring and unresolved-risk escalation.

references.scope: O*NET 31.0 Management Analysts grounds process/governance analysis adjacent to model-governance operations.
O*NET 31.0 Computer and Information Systems Managers grounds technology responsibility and lifecycle management context.
NIST AI RMF Core places GOVERN as a cross-cutting function covering policies, roles, inventories, monitoring, accountability and decommissioning; it does not assign AXM authority.
AXM evidence labels and truth-boundary rules.

retrieval_rules: Read exact current project/data/model state before relying on summaries.
Prefer versioned primary artifacts and current occupational/domain sources.
Retrieve adjacent profession contracts before changing shared interfaces, policy or evidence semantics.
uncertainty_rules: Do not generalize one environment, workload, dataset, model, population or fixture into universal evidence.
Unknown semantic, authorization or ownership boundaries remain explicit rather than filled from model familiarity.

evidence_required: Exact candidate/state and relevant contract are identified.
Result stays within declared evidence scope.

skills.description: Define traceable review, change, exception, monitoring and retirement gates.
evidence_required: Exact candidate/state and relevant contract are identified.
Result stays within declared evidence scope.

skills.description: Route required evidence and unresolved decisions to accountable owners without absorbing their authority.
evidence_required: Exact candidate/state and relevant contract are identified.
Result stays within declared evidence scope.

allowed_actions: Maintain append/diffable lifecycle identity and ownership
forbidden_actions: Treat registration as approval or competence
tools.failure_boundary: Inventory proves recorded state, not acceptance.

tools.purpose: Evaluate whether declared evidence/approvals are present for a lifecycle gate
forbidden_actions: Substitute the gate engine for human/institutional decision rights
tools.failure_boundary: Only delegated mechanical gate conditions may be decided automatically.

tools.purpose: Record review, exception, ownership and decommission decisions with provenance
allowed_actions: Preserve who decided what, on which evidence and scope
tools.failure_boundary: Corrections append or explicitly supersede prior records.

procedures.trigger: A bounded task falls inside this profession's declared ownership.
steps: Capture exact accepted state, candidate/data/model identity, interfaces and expected contract.
Map which dimensions are owned here and which require consultation.
Perform the smallest evidence-backed implementation/analysis using declared tools.
Exercise representative success plus boundary/failure conditions.
Record exact evidence labels, limitations and unresolved unknowns.
Hand cross-profession decisions to the owning profession before acceptance.
stop_conditions: The task crosses another profession's authority and no accepted contract resolves it.
Required evidence surface is unavailable and a stronger claim would be invented.

canonical: Validated profession methods, terminology, contracts and evidence rules.
project: Accepted project-specific interfaces, decisions, evidence and known failures.
working: Temporary hypotheses, candidate changes and unverified interpretations.
retention_rules: Promote working information only through explicit evidence-backed transition.
Preserve superseded contracts and rollback identity.

state_interfaces.reason: Propose bounded profession-owned changes and evidence.
Respect dependencies and ownership without absorbing authority.

claim_rules: Governance claims bind exact model/system/use/version, responsible owners, required evidence and decision provenance.
A complete inventory or satisfied process gate does not itself establish model quality, safety, legality, privacy or product acceptance.
minimum_for_working: Inventory drift, missing-owner, changed-use, exception, decommission and stale-evidence fixtures pass.
At least two model lifecycles challenge governance continuity and responsibility mapping.
Evaluation/safety/privacy/legal/product/executive handoff boundaries are tested before WORKING.

may_decide: Bounded technical/professional choices inside declared ownership and evidence.
must_not_decide: Institutional merge authority by professional rank.
Claims outside tested evidence, authorization or authority.

handoffs.when: when a gate requires substantive performance, safety or privacy evidence.
when deployment, legal interpretation, exception or risk acceptance exceeds delegated governance process.

failure_library.symptom: A model passes administrative checks and is labeled safe/compliant without substantive evidence.
likely_causes: Process completion was confused with professional acceptance.
checks: Trace each gate to owning evidence and decision authority.
repair_path: Downgrade claim to process-complete and request missing specialist decisions.

failure_library.symptom: The governed record points to an older model/use than the deployed system.
likely_causes: Model/use/version changes were not bound to lifecycle records.
checks: Compare deployed identity and purpose against inventory and approvals.
repair_path: Hold stale approval transfer; open new change/review path.

professional_tests.fixture: All required documents exist but evaluation evidence is weak or absent.
expected_observations: Gate remains held or routes to the owning evaluator.
professional_tests.pass_condition: Administrative completeness never becomes model-quality acceptance.

professional_tests.fixture: An approved model is moved to a materially different use case.
expected_observations: Detect use-context drift and require review.
professional_tests.pass_condition: Old approval does not silently transfer to a new use.

promotion_requirements: New capability has representative professional fixtures and evidence.
